BiblicalUsage: Ra'avah is the sight of the eyes — the beholding. The Preacher says when goods increase, they are increased that eat them, and what good is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding of them with their eyes? The rich man gets nothing from his wealth but the sight of it.
TheologicalSignificance: What strikes me is that this verse unmasks wealth: if all it buys is the sight of it, it was never worth the chasing.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
